design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a "randomized double-blinded, placebo-controlled, longitudinal intervention trial" in which "Students of each sex were assigned randomly to the different intervention arms" (three arms: placebo, FeSO4+citrate, NaFe-EDTA).

domain_judgments.rationale: Random allocation (apparently stratified by sex) is stated and baseline characteristics (age, sex, school, hb, SF, CRP, weight, height, BMI) did not differ significantly between arms, but no information is given on the method of sequence generation or on allocation concealment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The study was designed as a randomized double-blinded, placebo-controlled, longitudinal intervention trial... Students of each sex were assigned randomly to the different intervention arms."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blinded with an identical-appearing placebo fish sauce, intake of all 114 doses was fully supervised and leftovers re-weighed, with no between-group differences in make-up doses, so deviations from the intended intervention are very unlikely to have affected the outcome.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Field workers distributed and fully supervised the ingestion of the meals mixed with the 3 varieties of fish sauce... All 137 students who completed the study received 114 dosings... All meals were fully consumed with no left-over."

domain_judgments.rationale: Only 3 of 140 participants (2.2%) dropped out with reasons given (two abandoned, one withdrawn for falling hb), leaving outcome data for ~98% of randomized participants; minor variation in per-analysis n (43–47 per arm) is small and unlikely to bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Three female subjects dropped out (= 2.2%); two of them abandoned and one was excluded when hb dropped to 59 g/L. Thus, data on 137 subjects were available for analysis"

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcomes (hb, serum ferritin, CRP) were objective laboratory measures obtained with standardized automated assays and internal quality controls, applied identically across arms, under double-blind conditions; morbidity was teacher-recorded but assessors were blinded to allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "hb concentration was analysed within 6 h of blood sampling (CELL-DYN® 3200 automated laboratory analyser; Abbott®; internal quality control material...)"

domain_judgments.rationale: An a priori hypothesis and sample size were stated but no trial registration or accessible protocol is cited, multiple outcomes and additional post hoc analyses (sex/school distribution, SF by menstrual status, "data not shown") are reported, and a non-significant end-of-study hb difference (p=0.09) is described in the text as "significantly higher", suggesting some flexibility in reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "hb concentrations in the two iron-fortified groups were significantly higher than in the placebo group at the end of the study (p = 0.09)"

overall_summary: This double-blind, placebo-controlled trial had strong intervention delivery/adherence control, minimal attrition and objective laboratory outcomes, but the randomization method and allocation concealment are not described and there is no registered protocol, with some inconsistent/post hoc reporting (e.g., a p=0.09 difference described as significant). Overall risk is therefore "some concerns", driven by domains 1 and 5.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes cluster random allocation of villages to intervention arms: "Nine villages in the Haizijie Region were randomly assigned to one of two groups," and the design is described as "a randomized, double-blinded, controlled intervention trial."

domain_judgments.rationale: Only nine clusters were allocated with no description of the sequence-generation method or allocation concealment, the arms appear geographically separated along a road, and baseline values of the primary outcome (hemoglobin) and of anthropometry differed significantly between arms in several subgroups, indicating imbalance beyond chance expectation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Nine villages in the Haizijie Region were randomly assigned to one of two groups... The two groups of villages were evenly distributed on either side of a small road." / "the height and weight of the fortified subjects were marginally significantly lower than those of the control subjects at the baseline survey" / baseline hemoglobin "133.4 ± 11.5* (486)" and "116.6 ± 10.3*** (417)"

domain_judgments.rationale: Blinding was plausible (organoleptically identical products, no store sales, no evidence of exchange between villages), but individual intake was unmeasured, who was blinded is not specified, and the analysis appears to be of available cases per visit rather than an intention-to-treat analysis of all allocated participants.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The subjects in the control group were given nonfortified soy sauce of the same brand and quality... The two sauces were reported to taste the same." / "The actual amount of soy sauce consumed for each age and sex subgroup is not available, because the cooking was done on a household basis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Attrition was substantial and markedly differential between arms (14% vs 6%; subgroup Ns fluctuate greatly, e.g. 486→357 men), with no sensitivity analysis or evidence that results were robust to missingness.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "the dropout rate for hemoglobin assays was 14% in the fortified group as a whole and 6% in the control group during the 18 months of intervention. The main reasons for dropping out were that some subjects were not available at the time of follow-up examinations or were working out of town."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory biomarkers measured identically in both arms with standards, duplicates and blind quality-control samples, making assessor influence unlikely despite non-venous capillary sampling at some time points.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Hemoglobin (cyanmethemoglobin method...), plasma ferritin (radio immunoassay kit...)... Analytical standards and blind samples were used in all laboratory analyses. Duplicate samples were analyzed."

domain_judgments.rationale: No pre-registration or analysis protocol is cited, results are reported across many age/sex subgroups and multiple time points with simple ANOVA that ignores the cluster (village) design and makes no adjustment for multiplicity, allowing selective emphasis of favourable comparisons.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Data analysis was conducted by analysis of variance (ANOVA) with the Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS)."

overall_summary: Overall risk of bias is high, driven by the randomization domain (only nine clusters allocated with no described sequence generation or concealment, geographically contiguous arms, and significant baseline differences in hemoglobin and anthropometry) and by substantial differential attrition (14% vs 6%) with no sensitivity analysis. Outcome measurement was objective and well standardized, but blinding details, individual intake data, cluster-appropriate analysis and pre-specification of analyses are lacking.

design_rationale: Families (clusters) were explicitly allocated by computer-generated random numbers to fortified or control masala, with coded (double-blind) product distribution: "The 264 families were divided by use of computer-generated random numbers into fortified (135 families) and control (129 families) groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation used computer-generated random numbers at the family level with coded masala packages (implying concealment), and the groups were reported as matched on key baseline Fe-status and demographic variables (baseline means in Table 1 similar).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The 264 families were divided by use of computer-generated random numbers into fortified (135 families) and control (129 families) groups... The fortified and unfortified groups were matched for age, parity, duration of menstruation, income, alcohol consumption, and initial Fe status."

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with coded packages and distribution errors were monitored (12 families received the wrong masala, with sensitivity analysis showing no change), but adherence/actual masala consumption was not quantified per participant and the analysis was effectively per-protocol among survivors rather than intention-to-treat with all randomized families.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Eight of the fortified families and four of the unfortified families were found in single episodes to be using the incorrect form of masala. Exclusion of these families from the final analysis did not alter the results."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory measures (Hb, transferrin saturation, ferritin) assessed identically in both groups with extensive standardization and quality control, and blinding of participants/staff makes assessor influence unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The study was conducted as a double-blind procedure, the fortified and unfortified masala being identified by means of a numbered code... steps were taken to ensure comparable results with standardized laboratory methods."

domain_judgments.rationale: 267 of 939 eligible participants (~27%) dropped out over 2 y (migration, refusal, death) and outcomes were analysed only in completers; although dropout numbers/reasons were said not to differ by group, no numerical comparison or sensitivity analysis accounting for missingness (which could be related to Fe status/health) is presented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "After 2 y of fortification, 672 subjects remained in the study. A total of 267 subjects dropped out of the study: 129 moved away from the area, 115 refused to participate further, and 23 died. There were no significant differences in the number or category of dropouts between the fortified and unfortified groups."

domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol or pre-registration is available, and although the primary outcome (Hb) and sample size were pre-specified, multiple outcome operationalizations (Hb, ferritin, transferrin saturation, derived body Fe stores, status categories), sex- and age-split analyses, numerous post hoc subgroup analyses, and one-tailed p values create scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Because the alternate hypothesis in all comparisons was that the mean of measurements in the fortified group was greater than that in the control group, one-tailed probabilities were reported."

overall_summary: Although this cluster-randomized, double-blind fortification trial had sound allocation and objective, well-standardized laboratory outcomes, roughly 27% of participants were lost over 2 years with completers-only analysis and no sensitivity analysis for missingness, which drives a high overall risk of bias. Additional concerns arise from unquantified adherence/masala intake and from the absence of a protocol alongside many outcome operationalizations, one-tailed tests, and post hoc subgroup analyses.

design_rationale: The paper explicitly describes a "randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled design" in which "the anemic women who met the inclusion criteria were randomly divided into 2 groups" receiving NaFeEDTA-fortified or non-fortified fish sauce.

domain_judgments.rationale: Randomization is asserted and baseline characteristics (anthropometry, diet, CRP, iron indices, parasites) were well balanced, but no detail is given on how the allocation sequence was generated or whether allocation was concealed (e.g., whether assignment within each of the 6 factories was done by an independent party).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The anemic women who met the inclusion criteria were randomly divided into 2 groups: the iron-fortified group ... and the control group"

domain_judgments.rationale: Masking was achieved with coded, identical bottles and compliance was monitored daily with near-identical numbers of servings consumed in both groups, but the analysis was not intention-to-treat: 15 non-completers and one additional participant (excluded post hoc for "excessive blood loss") were removed from the analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Of the 137 women who completed the study, one woman in the control group was excluded from the data analysis because of excessive blood loss (based on estimated body iron)."

domain_judgments.rationale: About 10.5% of randomized women (16/152) lacked final outcome data, and loss was unequal between arms (12 from the iron-fortified group vs 4 from the control group); the authors show that dropouts did not differ at baseline, which mitigates but does not eliminate concern about differential attrition and reasons for dropout.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Fifteen women did not complete the study ... Initial nutritional status and iron status were not significantly different between the women who dropped out of the study and those who were included in the data analysis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes were objective laboratory biomarkers (hemoglobin, serum ferritin, transferrin receptor, CRP) measured identically in both groups with duplicate analyses, quality-control materials, and central/overseas laboratories under a double-masked design, so assessor knowledge could not plausibly bias results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Samples were analyzed in duplicate, and the analysis was repeated if the results differed by > 5%... SF and TfR were measured in duplicate at the Division of Hematology, Kansas University Medical Center"

domain_judgments.rationale: A principal hypothesis (hemoglobin) and an a priori sample-size calculation are stated and the analysis plan is described, but there is no trial registration or accessible protocol, and numerous secondary iron-status operationalizations (SF, TfR, TfR:SF, calculated body iron, ID, IDA, change scores) are reported, leaving some scope for selective reporting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "The principal hypothesis was that the women in the iron-fortified group would have higher hemoglobin concentrations at the end of the study period than would the women in the control group."

overall_summary: This double-masked, placebo-controlled trial used objective, centrally measured biomarker outcomes with balanced baseline characteristics and high monitored compliance, but details of sequence generation and allocation concealment are absent, the analysis was per-protocol (with ~10% differential attrition and one post hoc exclusion), and no pre-registered protocol is available. These issues yield "some concerns" overall, with no domain judged high risk.

design_rationale: Although the text states anaemic students were "randomly assigned to three treatment groups", the Results show allocation was in fact by school (school 1 = control, school 2 = low-NaFeEDTA, school 3 = high-NaFeEDTA) with no description of any random sequence generation; allocation therefore appears to be a quasi-experimental cluster (school-level) assignment rather than true randomization.

domain_judgments.rationale: Intervention was confounded with school (and thus cafeteria diet, sex distribution and baseline anaemia prevalence of 13.5%, 22.6% and 11.0%, plus clearly unbalanced baseline serum iron of 97.7 vs 73.1 vs 80.5 µg/dL), and no adjustment for these cluster-level or baseline imbalances was performed.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: school 1, 55 boys and 47 girls in the control group ... school 2, 39 boys and 63 girls in the low-NaFeEDTA group ... school 3, 61 boys and 39 girls in the high-NaFeEDTA group

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of participants into the study
domain_judgments.rationale: Participants were selected by uniform anaemia screening criteria applied at all three schools and enrolled at the start of follow-up, but the whole-school basis of condition assignment and the unexplained reduction from 304 enrolled to 240 analysed raises some concern about differential selection into the analysed groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Among the 4022 eligible students in the three selected middle schools, 4008 students were available.

domain_judgments.rationale: Interventions (non-fortified, 1 mg Fe/mL, 4 mg Fe/mL soy sauce) were clearly defined, prospectively administered and documented, so misclassification of exposure status is unlikely.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 5 mL of soy sauce was administered daily to each subject at lunch in the form of soy sauce soup for a period of 3 months ... detailed information on the soy sauce consumption of each subject was recorded on a consumption sheet.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias due to deviations from intended interventions
domain_judgments.rationale: Adherence was directly supervised, but the study reports no blinding of participants, staff or schools (the authors note only Ballot's earlier trial was double-blinded), and co-interventions such as differences in cafeteria diet or iron supplementation outside the trial are not reported or controlled.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: the soup was prepared in the school cafeteria and consumed by the subjects under complete supervision from the teachers

domain_judgments.rationale: About 21% of the 304 assigned participants (102/102/100 per school versus 81/82/77 analysed) are absent from the outcome tables with no explanation, no comparison of completers versus dropouts and no intention-to-treat or sensitivity analysis.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Three hundred and four students (155 boys and 149 girls) were diagnosed as anaemic and assigned to one of the three treatment groups ... Control 81 ... Low NaFeEDTA 82 ... High NaFeEDTA 77

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcomes are objective, standardized laboratory biomarkers measured identically across groups with quality control, but no blinding of laboratory or field assessors to group allocation is reported, and Hb was measured on fingertip blood in an unblinded setting.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Haemoglobin concentration was determined by the cyanomethemoglobin assay ... Quality-control serum samples with a known concentration (127 g/L) were provided by the Shanghai Institute of Clinical Examination.

domain_judgments.domain_name: Bias in selection of the reported result
domain_judgments.rationale: No protocol registration or pre-specified primary outcome is available, multiple iron-status outcomes and time points are reported with internally inconsistent/erroneous statistical statements (e.g. "Serum iron concentrations did change significantly ... in the control group"), and no statistical methods section describes the planned analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: the parameters measured were not changed remarkably within the 3-month intervention in the control group (P < 0.05)

overall_summary: Despite the claim of random assignment, treatment groups corresponded exactly to the three schools, so the intervention is confounded with school-level diet, sex composition and baseline iron status (serious confounding), and roughly 21% of assigned participants are unaccounted for in the analysis tables without explanation (serious missing-data bias). With additional moderate concerns about lack of blinding, selection into the analysed sample and absent pre-specification/statistical methods, the study is at serious overall risk of bias.

design_rationale: Cluster-randomized, double-blind trial: "Villages (n = 21) located in one of 2 communes were randomly divided into 2 groups to receive either unfortified (Group C) or fortified ... fish sauce", with randomly selected households within villages invited to the evaluation protocol.

domain_judgments.rationale: Allocation was random at the village level but the sequence-generation method and allocation concealment are not described, only 21 clusters were randomized, and baseline parasite prevalences differed significantly between groups (though key baseline variables—age, BMI, diet, Hb, SF—were balanced).
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Villages (n = 21) located in one of 2 communes were randomly divided into 2 groups to receive either unfortified (Group C) or fortified (9 mmol Fe/L as NaFeEDTA, Group F) fish sauce"; "The prevalences of Ascaris lumbricoides and hookworm infections were significantly higher in subgroup C."

domain_judgments.rationale: Participants and deliverers were blinded (visually identical fortified vs unfortified sauce in identical wrapped bottles), supply and consumption were monitored equally in both arms, retailers agreed not to sell competing sauce, and an intention-to-treat analysis was used.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "a double-blind intervention with randomization by village"; "Data were analyzed using SAS version 8.2 (SAS) on an intention-to-treat basis."

domain_judgments.rationale: Nearly one third of participants were lost by 18 months (balanced across arms and attributed to seasonal labor migration), and although a multivariate comparison of baseline characteristics of completers vs non-completers was non-significant (P = 0.14) and mixed models using all available data were applied, no sensitivity analysis for informative missingness was presented.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "A total of 188 women, 99 in Group C and 89 in Group F (32.6% of the whole sample) were lost to follow-up."

domain_judgments.rationale: Hemoglobin and serum ferritin are objective laboratory biomarkers measured identically in both arms with documented quality control, and the double-blind design makes assessor influence implausible.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Samples were analyzed in duplicate and the analysis repeated if the results differed by >5%"; "Quality control was monitored by analyzing 10% of the samples in duplicate. The CV was 4.7%."

domain_judgments.rationale: No trial registration or publicly available pre-specified analysis plan is cited, and the pre-specified primary outcome (body iron stores via transferrin receptor:SF ratio) was abandoned and replaced by hemoglobin/serum ferritin outcomes, raising the possibility of outcome-selection bias despite the transparent explanation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: "Sample size was estimated on the basis of an increase in body iron store as the primary outcome indicator... However, due to technical problems the serum transferrin receptor levels were considered to be unreliable. Therefore, they are not reported."

overall_summary: This double-blind cluster-randomized trial had strong intervention delivery, blinding, ITT analysis, and objective, quality-controlled laboratory outcomes, but concerns remain in three domains: unreported randomization/concealment mechanics with few clusters and some baseline imbalance in parasite prevalence, 32.6% loss to follow-up without sensitivity analysis, and replacement of the pre-specified primary outcome (body iron stores) with hemoglobin/serum ferritin in the absence of a registered protocol. No domain reached high risk, so the overall judgment is some concerns.
